title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 'Teichmülleries' notes study the genus-1 (and closely related genus-0, four-point) Teichmüller modular groups and their finite-index subgroups. This page appears to work out a lattice of finite-index subgroups of a group M, the (possibly extended) modular group of type (1,1) or the related (0,4) group, and to compute the corresponding finite quotients. Several identifications below are interpretive (see errors).

(1) Top-left square of inclusions. Horizontally: M^!_0 ⊂(2) M^! ⊂(6) M. Each of these contains a ° version with index 4: M^{!°}_0 ⊂ M^{!°} ⊂ M°. The ° subgroups map onto 1 —2— μ, with μ = {±1}. The total index of M^{!°}_0 in M is 2·6·4 = 48, which is the order of SL(2,Z/4Z). Read this way, M^{!°}_0 is a level-4-type congruence subgroup (kernel of reduction mod 4). The index 6 = |SL(2,F_2)| = |S_3| corresponds to a level-2 structure; the indices 2 come from sign/orientation characters with values in μ.

(2) The formula M^{!°}_0 ≃ M(0)°·Π_0, contained in M(0)·S^+ (inclusion indices written 4 and 12), compares genus 1 with genus 0, four points. Here M(0) is presumably the four-pointed genus-0 modular group; its pure part is free of rank 2. Π_0 is presumably the Klein four-group V_4 ⊂ S_4, and S^+ presumably the alternating group A_4. This recalls the classical facts:
- Mod(0,4) ≅ PSL(2,Z) ⋉ V_4;
- S_4/V_4 ≅ S_3 ≅ SL(2,F_2);
- the elliptic involution identifies the (1,1) and (0,4) pictures.
The map M → S/Π_0 × μ, labelled (φ, ε_3), is then 'permutation of the three 2-torsion points (S_4/V_4 = S_3)' times a sign character. A further map M → S_3×μ×μ, partly struck through, is followed by M → ... → S_3×μ×μ.

(3) The pencilled prism (left) and the inked prism (right). These are the subgroup lattice generated by three conjugate index-2 refinements, decorated ', '', ''' (one per choice of 2-torsion datum / nontrivial character), together with the !, °, _0 decorations. Edges carry indices 2 and 6. The resulting quotient is M/M^{!°} ≃ S_3×μ×μ (order 24 = 6·4). M/M^{!°}_0 is then compared with level-4 groups via 1 → K → SL(2,Z/4Z) → GL(2,Z/4Z) → (Z/4Z)^* → 1. The order counts are |SL(2,Z/4Z)| = 48, the kernel of SL(2,Z/4Z) → SL(2,Z/2Z) = S_3 has order 8 (48/8 = 6), and |GL(2,Z/4Z)| = 6·16 = 96. The marginal '6 Sl(2,Z/12Z)' presumably refers to the level-12 / abelianization Z/12 of SL(2,Z).

(4) D_ρ, D_σ are the decomposition (stabilizer) subgroups at the two elliptic points ρ = e^{2πi/3} and σ = i (orders 6 and 4 in SL(2,Z)). The final line M''!_0 ∩ N*_ρ = Z*''!_{ρ,0} records that intersecting a particular finite-index subgroup with the normalizer of the order-3/6 elliptic subgroup gives the corresponding centralizer-type subgroup. This is the kind of local bookkeeping needed to describe the tower's 'points at infinity/elliptic points' at each level.

Purpose: build the low-level (levels 2 and 4) part of the genus-1 / genus-0 Teichmüller tower as a finite lattice of subgroups with explicit quotients, as input for the Galois-action / Teichmüller-tower program later sketched in Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: If M is GL(2,Z) (the extended (1,1) modular group), M cannot surject onto S_3×μ×μ. GL(2,Z)^ab ≅ (Z/2)^2, while the abelianization of S_3×μ×μ is (Z/2)^3. The same obstruction holds for SL(2,Z), whose abelianization is Z/12, and for PGL(2,Z)⋉V_4. This is consistent with the struck-through 'M → S_3×μ×μ'. The later identification of a quotient (underlined M)/M^{!°} ≃ S_3×μ×μ must therefore refer to a group with larger abelianization, or to a non-normal subgroup/coset space, or else needs a semidirect product. It cannot be verified from the page.
The indices '∩4, ∩12' under M(0)°·Π_0 ⊂ M(0)·S^+ do not match the natural count [A_4 : V_4] = 3. Either S^+ / Π_0 mean something else, or the 12 is an order rather than an index. This is ambiguous.

ideas.what: Lattice of finite-index subgroups of the genus-1 modular group at levels 2 and 4, with explicit quotients S_3×μ×μ and SL(2,Z/4Z), GL(2,Z/4Z) (orders 48, 96 = 6·16)
ideas.modern_name: Congruence subgroups Γ(2), Γ(4) and finite quotients of SL(2,Z)/GL(2,Z); level structures on M_{1,1}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the genus-1 tower and level structures in general terms

ideas.what: Comparison of the genus-1 group with the four-pointed genus-0 group via Klein four-group V_4 ⊂ S_4 and S_4/V_4 ≅ S_3
ideas.modern_name: Mod(0,4) ≅ PSL(2,Z) ⋉ (Z/2)^2; elliptic involution relating M_{1,1} and M_{0,4}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; standard in mapping class group literature (e.g. Farb–Margalit Primer)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (genus 0/1 two-dimensional modular multiplicities, discussed qualitatively)

ideas.what: Decomposition groups D_ρ, D_σ at elliptic points and their normalizer/centralizer intersections with finite-index subgroups
ideas.modern_name: Stabilizers of elliptic points / inertia at orbifold points of M_{1,1}; 'tangential base points' bookkeeping in the Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for the groups; the tower viewpoint is Grothendieck's, later developed by Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps

deep.surprise_reason: The page is working bookkeeping of indices and finite quotients of low-level (2 and 4) subgroups of the genus-1/genus-0 modular groups. All of this is classical congruence-subgroup and mapping-class-group material. There is no new result or connection beyond what the published Teichmüller-tower literature contains.
transcription_corrections: The upper-right horizontal label in the second row of the top-left diagram is a struck '6' (index 6), i.e. M^{!°} —6— M°.
'S/Π_0 × μ' is written with the gothic S (probably the symmetric group S_4) divided by Π_0. It is likely S_4/V_4 ≅ S_3, not a generic quotient.
In 'M → S_3 × μ × μ' (left, lower) the target is partially struck through, with arrows down to a rewritten 'S_3×μ×μ'.
The right-hand quotient reads 'M̲/M̲^{!°} ≃ S_3×μ×μ → 1', with M underlined; a second line reads 'M̲/M̲^{!°}_0 →'.

Under SL(2,Z/4Z) the annotations are '48' (with a struck repeat), then ')8' and a downward arrow to 'SL(2,Z/2Z)' with 6. The text shows SL(2,Z/12Z), but SL(2,Z/2Z) fits the arithmetic 48/8 = 6. '6.16' is the order of GL(2,Z/4Z).
